albums.title: In the Wee Small Hours
albums.summary: Frank Sinatra's album of slow ballads about loneliness, arranged by Nelson Riddle. It was one of the first pop LPs built around a single mood.

cousins.why: Late-night records that hold one mood from start to finish
Quiet albums about heartbreak and solitude

albums.title: Elvis Presley
albums.summary: Elvis' first album, with 'Blue Suede Shoes', was the first rock and roll album to top the Billboard chart.

cousins.why: A pop event that reshaped youth culture

albums.title: Three Ragas
albums.summary: Ravi Shankar's first LP of extended ragas, which helped bring Indian classical music to Western listeners.

cousins.why: Improvisation over modes instead of chord changes

albums.title: Birth of the Cool
albums.summary: Collects the 1949 and 1950 nonet sessions arranged by Gil Evans, Gerry Mulligan and John Lewis. It set out a calmer, arranged alternative to bebop.

cousins.why: Low-key, late-night mood sustained across a whole LP

albums.title: The Best of Muddy Waters
albums.summary: A collection of Muddy Waters' early Chess singles, including 'Hoochie Coochie Man' and 'Rollin' Stone'. It became a key record for the young British musicians who started the blues boom.

cousins.why: Plain, tough records about hard lives sung without decoration

albums.title: Kind of Blue
albums.summary: Miles Davis' sextet with John Coltrane and Bill Evans improvising over modes instead of fast chord changes. It is the best-selling jazz album and a reference point for musicians in every genre.

influencedBy.why: Davis carried the space and restraint of the nonet sessions into a looser, modal setting.

cousins.why: Unhurried, spacious music that became a perennial best seller
Quiet, understated playing that still feels intense

albums.title: Mingus Ah Um
albums.summary: Charles Mingus mixed gospel, blues and swing with sharp political edge, as on 'Fables of Faubus'.

cousins.why: Dense, political, and full of overlapping voices
Rowdy, genre-hopping records with political bite

albums.title: Chuck Berry Is on Top
albums.summary: A collection of Chuck Berry hits including 'Johnny B. Goode', 'Maybellene' and 'Roll Over Beethoven'. His riffs and lyrics became rock's grammar.

cousins.why: Defined the vocabulary of its genre
Showmen whose moves and riffs were copied everywhere

albums.title: Chega de Saudade
albums.summary: João Gilberto's debut, with songs by Antônio Carlos Jobim, introduced bossa nova's soft voice and syncopated guitar.

albums.title: King of the Delta Blues Singers
albums.summary: Columbia's LP reissue of Robert Johnson's 1936 and 1937 recordings. It introduced his songs to a new generation of folk and rock players.

cousins.why: One voice and one guitar, sparse and haunted
Solo acoustic songs that later players treated as a songbook

albums.title: Howlin' Wolf
albums.summary: Known as the 'rocking chair album', it collects Wolf's Chess sides such as 'Spoonful', 'Back Door Man' and 'The Red Rooster'. Many of its songs became rock standards.

cousins.why: Heavy, menacing riffs built around a huge voice
Raw, gravel-voiced music with no polish

albums.title: El Rey Bravo
albums.summary: Tito Puente's album that introduced 'Oye Como Va'.

albums.title: The Freewheelin' Bob Dylan
albums.summary: Dylan's second album, with 'Blowin' in the Wind' and 'A Hard Rain's a-Gonna Fall', made him the leading songwriter of the folk revival.

influencedBy.why: In Chronicles, Dylan describes how hearing this Robert Johnson LP in 1961 changed the way he wrote.

cousins.why: Solo acoustic songs that later players treated as a songbook

albums.title: With the Beatles
albums.summary: The Beatles' second album mixed originals with covers of Motown and Chuck Berry songs.

influencedBy.why: The band covers Berry's 'Roll Over Beethoven', a staple of their early live sets.

cousins.why: 1960s records built around strong vocals and tight bands

albums.title: Night Beat
albums.summary: A quiet, late-night blues album recorded with a small combo, showing Sam Cooke at his most intimate.

albums.title: Live at the Apollo
albums.summary: James Brown financed this live recording himself; it was a surprise hit and set the standard for live soul.

cousins.why: A live album where the crowd is part of the show

albums.title: The Rolling Stones
albums.summary: The Stones' debut was mostly American blues and R&B covers played with raw energy.

influencedBy.why: Keith Richards has said Mick Jagger was carrying Muddy Waters records when they met in 1961; the band named itself after 'Rollin' Stone'.
Berry's songs and riffs were central to the early Stones, who covered 'Carol' here.

cousins.why: Raw, loud reworkings of older records
A tough band sound against the polished mainstream

albums.title: Presenting the Fabulous Ronettes Featuring Veronica
albums.summary: The Ronettes' only original album, including 'Be My Baby', produced by Phil Spector with his Wall of Sound.

cousins.why: The Jesus and Mary Chain buried Spector-style pop under noise

albums.title: Getz/Gilberto
albums.summary: João Gilberto with saxophonist Stan Getz and Jobim on piano, including 'The Girl from Ipanema'. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

influencedBy.why: Gilberto carried his bossa nova style to an American jazz audience.
Stan Getz came out of the cool jazz movement Birth of the Cool helped start.

cousins.why: Quiet, cool records that became huge sellers

albums.title: Live at the Regal
albums.summary: B.B. King recorded live in Chicago before an enthusiastic crowd. Guitarists studied it for his phrasing, vibrato and showmanship.

cousins.why: A live album that captures a performer working a crowd at full intensity
A live record where the audience is part of the music

albums.title: Pastel Blues
albums.summary: Nina Simone's spare blues album, including her version of 'Strange Fruit' and the ten-minute 'Sinnerman'.

cousins.why: Kanye West sampled its 'Strange Fruit' on Yeezus; both are stark, confrontational records about race
Unguarded, personal singing over sparse settings

albums.title: A Love Supreme
albums.summary: A four-part suite Coltrane wrote as a devotional offering. It became the model for spiritual jazz.

influencedBy.why: Coltrane's modal playing grew out of his time on the Kind of Blue sessions.
Coltrane studied Indian classical music and Ravi Shankar's recordings in this period, later naming his son Ravi.

cousins.why: A long-form spiritual statement from a whole band

albums.title: Bringing It All Back Home
albums.summary: Half electric, half acoustic, this album took Dylan into rock and included 'Mr. Tambourine Man'.

influencedBy.why: Dylan moved from topical folk to surreal, electric songs.
Dylan said hearing the Beatles showed him where music was going, and he went electric soon after.

cousins.why: Mixing old and new styles to change a genre

albums.title: Highway 61 Revisited
albums.summary: Dylan's first fully electric album, opening with 'Like a Rolling Stone'. It changed what rock lyrics could do.

influencedBy.why: Dylan went fully electric after the half-electric Bringing It All Back Home.

cousins.why: A sweeping tour of American roots music with sharp lyrics

albums.title: Mr. Tambourine Man
albums.summary: The Byrds' debut put Dylan songs to Beatles-style harmonies and Roger McGuinn's 12-string guitar, inventing folk rock.

influencedBy.why: The title track is a Dylan song from that album, electrified.
McGuinn adopted the 12-string Rickenbacker after seeing George Harrison play one, and the group built on Beatles harmonies.

cousins.why: Bright, melodic music that opened a new lane in its genre

albums.title: Rubber Soul
albums.summary: The Beatles' first album conceived as a whole, with folk rock textures and more personal lyrics.

influencedBy.why: Lennon's writing in this period, as on 'Norwegian Wood', was openly shaped by Dylan.
Harrison said the Byrds' sound influenced songs such as 'If I Needed Someone'.

cousins.why: Gentle, inventive albums that moved a genre away from its rougher roots

albums.title: Otis Blue: Otis Redding Sings Soul
albums.summary: Otis Redding's Stax album with 'Respect' and covers of Sam Cooke and the Rolling Stones.

influencedBy.why: Redding covered three Sam Cooke songs here, recorded months after Cooke's death.

cousins.why: Remaking contemporaries' songs; Redding covers '(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction' here

albums.title: Pet Sounds
albums.summary: Brian Wilson's orchestral, introspective album, built in the studio with session players. It changed how albums were made.

influencedBy.why: Brian Wilson said Rubber Soul made him want to make an album with no filler.
Wilson was obsessed with Phil Spector's production of 'Be My Baby' and used his Wall of Sound methods.

cousins.why: A studio obsessive's maximal, layered masterpiece
Lavish, perfectionist studio records made with session players

albums.title: Revolver
albums.summary: The Beatles' studio experiments with tape loops, backwards guitar and Indian music, ending on 'Tomorrow Never Knows'.

influencedBy.why: The band pushed further into studio experiment after Rubber Soul.
George Harrison studied Ravi Shankar's music and wrote 'Love You To' in that style.

cousins.why: Tape loops and sampling used as composition

albums.title: Born Under a Bad Sign
albums.summary: Albert King backed by Booker T. & the M.G.'s at Stax, mixing blues guitar with soul grooves. Its title track and bending style were copied widely.

cousins.why: The Stax house band's grooves behind a commanding lead
Simple, heavy guitar bends over a locked groove

albums.title: John Wesley Harding
albums.summary: A quiet, biblical-sounding album recorded in Nashville that pushed back against psychedelia.

influencedBy.why: Dylan pared back the electric sound to short, parable-like songs.

cousins.why: A quiet, sharp turn away from what the artist was expected to make

albums.title: The Velvet Underground & Nico
albums.summary: Produced in name by Andy Warhol, its songs about drugs and street life sold poorly but influenced punk and indie rock.

cousins.why: Bleak, urban music that grew in stature slowly
Abrasive records that divided listeners at release and later became templates

albums.title: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
albums.summary: The Beatles' studio album framed as a performance by a fictional band. It made the album the main art form of rock.

influencedBy.why: Paul McCartney has said Pet Sounds was the main inspiration for Sgt. Pepper.
The band extended the studio experiments of Revolver.

cousins.why: Ambitious genre collisions on a big canvas

albums.title: Are You Experienced
albums.summary: Hendrix's debut used feedback, distortion and wild technique to remake the electric guitar.

influencedBy.why: Hendrix drew on Chicago blues, regularly playing Howlin' Wolf's 'Killing Floor' live.

cousins.why: Electric experiments that rewrote a genre
Guitar sound as the main event

albums.title: I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You
albums.summary: Aretha Franklin's Atlantic debut, recorded partly in Muscle Shoals, including her version of 'Respect'.

influencedBy.why: Franklin's 'Respect' reworks Otis Redding's song from Otis Blue.

cousins.why: A powerful woman's voice demanding respect

albums.title: At Folsom Prison
albums.summary: Johnny Cash's live album recorded for prisoners at Folsom State Prison. It revived his career and fixed his image as an outsider.

cousins.why: A live record where the crowd is part of the song
Stories of crime and punishment told without apology

albums.title: Mama Tried
albums.summary: Merle Haggard's album with the autobiographical title track about his time in prison. It defined the Bakersfield style of twangy, plain country.

cousins.why: Autobiographical songs about trouble and a mother's love
Songs from people on the wrong side of the law

albums.title: Electric Ladyland
albums.summary: A double album Hendrix produced himself, including his version of 'All Along the Watchtower'.

influencedBy.why: Hendrix took the sound of his debut into longer, studio-built pieces.
Hendrix's 'All Along the Watchtower' comes from this Dylan album.

cousins.why: Long electric jams shaped in the studio

albums.title: Sweetheart of the Rodeo
albums.summary: With Gram Parsons, the Byrds made a straight country album in Nashville, an early country rock landmark.

influencedBy.why: The Byrds shifted from Dylan-style folk rock to country, keeping their harmonies.

cousins.why: Musicians adopting another genre's style with care

albums.title: Wheels of Fire
albums.summary: Cream's double album, half studio and half live, with long improvised blues jams like 'Spoonful'.

influencedBy.why: Cream covered the title song of Albert King's album.
The live set features a long version of 'Spoonful' from this Howlin' Wolf album.
Eric Clapton has named Live at the Regal as a record he studied closely, and its phrasing runs through his Cream solos.

cousins.why: Extended improvisation for a rock audience
Blues guitar at length in front of a crowd

albums.title: Os Mutantes
albums.summary: Os Mutantes' debut mixed Brazilian music with Beatles-style psychedelia and studio pranks.

influencedBy.why: The band was openly inspired by the Beatles' psychedelic studio work.

albums.title: Karma
albums.summary: Built around the 32-minute 'The Creator Has a Master Plan', Sanders' album pushed Coltrane's spiritual direction further.

influencedBy.why: Sanders played in Coltrane's last bands and continued the devotional approach of A Love Supreme.

cousins.why: Long, meditative pieces meant to be lived in
Cosmic, spiritual sound with free passages

albums.title: Led Zeppelin
albums.summary: Led Zeppelin's debut turned blues covers and originals into loud, heavy rock and set the template for hard rock.

influencedBy.why: Critics place it in direct line from Cream's amplified, extended blues rock.
Critics tie its heavy, distorted blues to the sound Hendrix had opened up.

cousins.why: Loud, riff-centered records that hit mainstream youth culture

albums.title: In the Court of the Crimson King
albums.summary: King Crimson's debut mixed jazz, classical and heavy rock with Mellotron, often called the first true prog album.

influencedBy.why: Critics see it as taking the art-rock ambition of Sgt. Pepper into longer, heavier forms.

cousins.why: Long, technical compositions with dramatic shifts

albums.title: Stand!
albums.summary: Sly and the Family Stone's mixed-race, mixed-gender band made funk, rock and soul into a utopian party.

influencedBy.why: Sly drew on James Brown's rhythmic funk.

albums.title: Bitches Brew
albums.summary: A double album of long electric jams edited by producer Teo Macero. It launched jazz fusion and the careers of many in its band.

influencedBy.why: Davis took the modal vamps of Kind of Blue and stretched them into long electric grooves.
Davis was listening closely to Sly Stone at the time and wanted the rhythmic drive of funk and rock.
Davis admired Hendrix and drew on his electric sound while moving toward fusion.

cousins.why: Thom Yorke cited it as a reference, and both build dread through texture
Long, edited jams that blur improvisation and studio construction

albums.title: Paranoid
albums.summary: Black Sabbath's second album, with 'Iron Man' and 'War Pigs', set the template for heavy metal.

influencedBy.why: Geezer Butler and Tony Iommi have cited Cream's heavy blues as a starting point.

cousins.why: Menacing riffs and a dark mood

albums.title: Coat of Many Colors
albums.summary: Dolly Parton's album with the title song about her mother sewing her a coat from rags. It showed her as a major songwriter.

cousins.why: A songwriter stepping fully into her own voice in 1971
Personal 1971 songs drawn from the writer's own life

albums.title: Blue
albums.summary: Joni Mitchell's spare, very personal album, often named the finest singer-songwriter record.

cousins.why: Raw personal detail in an intimate setting
A young writer's precise, private observations

albums.title: Tago Mago
albums.summary: Can's double album of long, edited improvisations over hypnotic drums. It influenced post-punk and electronic music.

influencedBy.why: Bassist Holger Czukay and the band cited the Velvet Underground's repetition as a model.

cousins.why: Edited jams that blur improvisation and composition

albums.title: What's Going On
albums.summary: Marvin Gaye's song cycle about war, poverty and the environment, made against Motown's wishes.

cousins.why: A Black American concept album about the state of the nation

albums.title: There's a Riot Goin' On
albums.summary: Sly Stone's dark, murky follow-up used drum machines and overdubs, turning away from the utopian sound of Stand!.

influencedBy.why: Sly turned the bright funk of Stand! into a darker, more personal sound.

albums.title: Tapestry
albums.summary: Carole King moved from writing hits for others to singing her own, and the album stayed on the charts for years.

cousins.why: A songwriter stepping into her own voice in 1971

albums.title: Pink Moon
albums.summary: Nick Drake's last album, just voice, guitar and one piano overdub. It sold little at first but grew into a cult classic.

cousins.why: Lonely, nocturnal music that found its audience slowly

albums.title: Exile on Main St.
albums.summary: Recorded in a French villa basement, this murky double album mixes rock, blues, country and gospel.

influencedBy.why: Keith Richards spent much of this period with Gram Parsons, and his country influence shows in songs like 'Sweet Virginia'.
The band returned to the blues and R&B roots of its early records.

albums.title: The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars
albums.summary: Bowie's concept album about an alien rock star made him a star and a model for persona-driven pop.

influencedBy.why: Bowie championed the Velvet Underground and wrote songs in their style.

cousins.why: A space-age alter ego at the center
A star building a stage persona around glamour and liberation

albums.title: Close to the Edge
albums.summary: Three long tracks, including the 18-minute title suite. A peak of symphonic prog.

influencedBy.why: Critics place it after Crimson's debut in building rock into long, classical-style suites.
Yes began as Beatles admirers, covering 'Every Little Thing' on their debut, and built on the Beatles' studio ambition.

cousins.why: A spiritually minded suite in movements

albums.title: The Harder They Come
albums.summary: Soundtrack to the Jimmy Cliff film, collecting songs by Cliff, Toots and the Maytals and Desmond Dekker. It introduced reggae to many outside Jamaica.

cousins.why: Stories of a man against the system

albums.title: Space Is the Place
albums.summary: Sun Ra and his Arkestra's soundtrack-era album built around his Afrofuturist ideas of space travel and Black liberation.

cousins.why: Afrofuturist space mythology as a frame for Black music

albums.title: Head Hunters
albums.summary: Hancock's funk-based band album, with synthesizers and the hit 'Chameleon'. It was the first jazz album to go platinum.

influencedBy.why: Hancock played in Davis' electric bands and carried their fusion ideas forward.
Hancock said Sly Stone's music made him want to play funk, and the album includes a track named 'Sly'.

albums.title: Honky Tonk Heroes
albums.summary: Waylon Jennings recorded mostly Billy Joe Shaver songs with his own band rather than Nashville session players. It became a blueprint for outlaw country.

cousins.why: Artists breaking from an industry system to make it their own way
A tough, band-driven sound against the polished mainstream

albums.title: The Dark Side of the Moon
albums.summary: Pink Floyd's concept album about madness and pressure, with seamless studio effects. It stayed on the Billboard chart for over 900 weeks.

influencedBy.why: Floyd recorded at Abbey Road alongside the Beatles and pushed the continuous, conceptual album further.

cousins.why: Unhurried music that became a perennial best seller
A continuous album held together by sound effects and theme

albums.title: Raw Power
albums.summary: Iggy and the Stooges' violent, chaotic album, mixed by David Bowie. It became a key proto-punk record.

influencedBy.why: Critics place the Stooges with the Velvets as the two main roots of punk, and both were championed by Bowie.

cousins.why: Chaos and aggression as the point

albums.title: Catch a Fire
albums.summary: The Wailers' first album for Island, with rock overdubs added in London, aimed at international rock audiences.

cousins.why: Political music with a smooth surface

albums.title: Autobahn
albums.summary: Kraftwerk's 22-minute title track about driving on the motorway brought synthesizer music to the charts.

cousins.why: A long, seamless piece of studio music
Driving as the album's central image

albums.title: Celia & Johnny
albums.summary: Celia Cruz with bandleader Johnny Pacheco on Fania, including 'Quimbara'. It helped define 1970s salsa.

influencedBy.why: Cruz had sung with Tito Puente, and the album builds on the New York mambo big band tradition.

cousins.why: A queen of her genre at full power

albums.title: Red Headed Stranger
albums.summary: A sparse concept album about a preacher on the run, recorded cheaply in Texas. It was a surprise hit and a high point of the outlaw movement.

cousins.why: Spare, story-driven albums made against expectations
A narrative concept album following one man's story

albums.title: Blood on the Tracks
albums.summary: Dylan's album about a failing marriage, with 'Tangled Up in Blue'. It is widely counted among his best.

cousins.why: Breakup albums that changed how their artists were heard
Albums made from a relationship's collapse

albums.title: Toys in the Attic
albums.summary: Aerosmith's breakthrough, with 'Walk This Way' and 'Sweet Emotion'.

influencedBy.why: Critics described Aerosmith as an American answer to the Rolling Stones from the start.

albums.title: Born to Run
albums.summary: Springsteen's breakthrough, packed with dense, Spector-style production and romantic songs about escape.

influencedBy.why: Springsteen said he wanted the record to sound like Phil Spector's productions.
Springsteen has described hearing 'Like a Rolling Stone' as a turning point, and early critics called him a new Dylan.

albums.title: Mothership Connection
albums.summary: Parliament's Afrofuturist funk album with 'Give Up the Funk'. Its grooves were sampled heavily in hip-hop.

influencedBy.why: George Clinton's space mythology followed Sun Ra's Afrofuturism.
Clinton's band included James Brown alumni like Bootsy Collins and Fred Wesley.

albums.title: Ramones
albums.summary: Fourteen fast, short songs in under thirty minutes. It set the template for punk rock.

influencedBy.why: The Ramones loved the Ronettes and later worked with Phil Spector.
The band drew on the Stooges' raw, loud attack.

cousins.why: Short, repetitive songs that spawned a whole scene

albums.title: Songs in the Key of Life
albums.summary: Stevie Wonder's double album, with 'Sir Duke' and 'Isn't She Lovely'.

influencedBy.why: Wonder took the creative control Gaye had won at Motown.

albums.title: Super Ape
albums.summary: Lee Perry's dense, murky dub album from his Black Ark studio, credited to the Upsetters.

cousins.why: The studio used as an instrument

albums.title: King Tubby Meets Rockers Uptown
albums.summary: King Tubby's dub mixes of Augustus Pablo's productions, a defining dub album of echo and bass.

cousins.why: Space and echo used as the music itself

albums.title: Zombie
albums.summary: Fela Kuti and Afrika 70's attack on Nigeria's military. The government raided his compound in response.

influencedBy.why: Fela built Afrobeat partly from James Brown's funk, which he heard in the late 1960s.

albums.title: Rumours
albums.summary: Made while the band's relationships were falling apart, it became one of the best-selling albums ever.

albums.title: Low
albums.summary: The first of Bowie's Berlin albums with Brian Eno, pairing broken funk songs with ambient instrumentals.

influencedBy.why: Bowie was listening to Kraftwerk and German electronic music at the time.
Bowie cited the German krautrock bands, including Can, as an influence on the Berlin records.

cousins.why: A star retreating into cold, electronic sounds
A sharp turn toward electronic textures

albums.title: Marquee Moon
albums.summary: Television's debut paired punk energy with long, interlocking guitar solos.

influencedBy.why: Critics place Television squarely in the Velvet Underground's New York line.

cousins.why: Long, lyrical solos over simple structures

albums.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols
albums.summary: The Sex Pistols' only studio album, built on scandal and aggression. It brought punk to the mainstream in Britain.

influencedBy.why: The Ramones' July 1976 London shows energized the British punk scene.
The band was steeped in the Stooges, covering their song 'No Fun', and Steve Jones drew on their guitar attack.

cousins.why: Records that shocked the establishment and sparked moral panic

albums.title: I Remember Yesterday
albums.summary: Donna Summer and Giorgio Moroder's album tracing pop history, ending with the fully synthesized 'I Feel Love'.

albums.title: Trans-Europe Express
albums.summary: Kraftwerk's album about European travel, with mechanical rhythms. It became a source for hip-hop and techno.

influencedBy.why: Kraftwerk developed the travel theme and electronic sound of Autobahn.

albums.title: Exodus
albums.summary: Recorded in London after an assassination attempt, with 'One Love', 'Jamming' and 'Three Little Birds'.

influencedBy.why: Marley continued the international reggae sound launched on Catch a Fire.

albums.title: Ambient 1: Music for Airports
albums.summary: Brian Eno's tape-loop pieces, meant to be heard in the background, gave the name and model for ambient music.

cousins.why: Quiet music that rewards close listening

albums.title: Unknown Pleasures
albums.summary: Joy Division's debut, produced by Martin Hannett, gave post-punk its cold, spacious sound.

influencedBy.why: The band first called itself Warsaw after 'Warszawa' from Low.
The band played Kraftwerk before shows and drew on its cold rhythm.

albums.title: London Calling
albums.summary: The Clash's double album took punk into reggae, rockabilly, ska and jazz.

influencedBy.why: The cover's pink and green lettering copies Elvis' debut album.
The Clash were steeped in Jamaican music and covered Toots' 'Pressure Drop', from this soundtrack.

albums.title: Risqué
albums.summary: Chic's album with 'Good Times', whose bassline became the basis of 'Rapper's Delight'.

cousins.why: Nile Rodgers' guitar at the center
Dance music built on a hypnotic bassline

albums.title: Off the Wall
albums.summary: Michael Jackson's first album with producer Quincy Jones, a polished mix of disco, funk and ballads.

influencedBy.why: Jackson admired Stevie Wonder, who co-wrote 'I Can't Help It' for the album.

cousins.why: Late-70s disco built on tight live musicianship

albums.title: Back in Black
albums.summary: AC/DC's tribute to Bon Scott with new singer Brian Johnson, produced by Mutt Lange. One of the best-selling albums ever.

influencedBy.why: Angus Young's riffs come from Chuck Berry, whose duck walk he also borrowed.

albums.title: Remain in Light
albums.summary: Produced by Brian Eno, Talking Heads built songs from layered, looping grooves.

influencedBy.why: David Byrne and Eno studied Fela Kuti's Afrobeat, and they used its interlocking polyrhythms.
Brian Eno produced it, and his tape-loop and layering methods shaped how the songs were built.

albums.title: British Steel
albums.summary: Judas Priest's leaner, punchier album with 'Breaking the Law'.

influencedBy.why: Judas Priest came out of the same Birmingham heavy rock scene, and Rob Halford has credited Sabbath with starting heavy metal.

albums.title: Ace of Spades
albums.summary: Motörhead's fast, loud album bridged punk and metal.

albums.title: Strait Country
albums.summary: George Strait's debut brought back Western swing and honky-tonk at the height of the urban cowboy era.

influencedBy.why: Strait has named Merle Haggard as a key model for his traditional sound.

cousins.why: An early-80s return to roots sounds
Faithful revival of older American styles

albums.title: Damaged
albums.summary: Black Flag's debut album, with Henry Rollins, defined American hardcore.

influencedBy.why: Black Flag sped up the Ramones' short, fast songs into hardcore.
Greg Ginn and the band came out of the punk wave the Sex Pistols started.

albums.title: The Number of the Beast
albums.summary: Iron Maiden's first album with Bruce Dickinson.

influencedBy.why: Maiden were part of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal that Priest defined.

albums.title: Thriller
albums.summary: Jackson and Quincy Jones' follow-up mixed pop, rock, funk and post-disco, and became the best-selling album of all time.

influencedBy.why: Jackson and Jones expanded the approach of Off the Wall with more rock and synth sounds.

cousins.why: Mid-80s crossover blockbusters mixing rock and funk
Records that raised the commercial ceiling of their genre

albums.title: Texas Flood
albums.summary: Stevie Ray Vaughan's debut, cut in a few days, brought loud electric blues back to the charts in the 1980s.

influencedBy.why: Vaughan built his string bending on Albert King's style and regularly cited King as his main model.
Vaughan named Jimi Hendrix as a central influence and drew on his tone and approach.

cousins.why: An early-80s return to roots sounds that had gone out of fashion
Guitar virtuosity as the center of the record

albums.title: Power, Corruption & Lies
albums.summary: New Order's second album fused post-punk guitars with drum machines and sequencers.

influencedBy.why: New Order drew directly on Kraftwerk's sequenced sound.
The band formed from Joy Division after Ian Curtis' death.

albums.title: Enter
albums.summary: Juan Atkins' Cybotron album, including 'Clear' and 'Techno City', was a key step toward Detroit techno.

influencedBy.why: Atkins has cited Kraftwerk as his main influence.

albums.title: Purple Rain
albums.summary: Prince's soundtrack mixed rock, funk and synth-pop and topped the charts.

influencedBy.why: Prince modeled his mixed-race, mixed-gender band on Sly and the Family Stone.

albums.title: Psychocandy
albums.summary: The Jesus and Mary Chain buried 1960s girl-group melodies under feedback.

influencedBy.why: The band took Phil Spector's girl-group pop and drenched it in noise.
The band's drone and feedback came from the Velvet Underground.

cousins.why: Tunes buried under abrasive, blown-out sound

albums.title: Hounds of Love
albums.summary: Kate Bush produced it herself in a home studio: one side of hit songs and one side of a conceptual suite, 'The Ninth Wave'.

influencedBy.why: Bush has named David Bowie as a formative influence on her theatrical approach.

cousins.why: A self-directed artist's dense, ambitious statement

albums.title: Master of Puppets
albums.summary: Metallica's third album, a peak of thrash.

influencedBy.why: Lars Ulrich was an avid Motörhead fan.
Metallica drew on the New Wave of British Heavy Metal.

cousins.why: Long, technical songs with dramatic shifts

albums.title: Reign in Blood
albums.summary: Produced by Rick Rubin, Slayer's 29-minute album is a landmark of extreme metal.

influencedBy.why: Slayer has named Judas Priest as an influence.

albums.title: Planet Rock: The Album
albums.summary: Collects 'Planet Rock' (1982) and other electro tracks with the Soulsonic Force, mixing Kraftwerk melodies with drum machines.

influencedBy.why: 'Planet Rock' borrows the melody of Kraftwerk's 'Trans-Europe Express'.

cousins.why: Electronic dance music with robotic sounds

albums.title: Raising Hell
albums.summary: Run-DMC's third album, produced with Rick Rubin, including 'Walk This Way' with Aerosmith.

influencedBy.why: 'Walk This Way' is a remake of Aerosmith's song from this album.

cousins.why: Raw, loud reworkings of older records

albums.title: Paid in Full
albums.summary: Eric B. & Rakim's debut introduced Rakim's complex internal rhymes and calm delivery.

cousins.why: Defined the vocabulary of its genre
Cool, controlled delivery that changed how a form was played

albums.title: Surfer Rosa
albums.summary: Pixies' first full album, recorded by Steve Albini, with loud-quiet dynamics and 'Where Is My Mind?'.

cousins.why: Loud, abrasive and odd, with a fierce cult following
Strange, jagged music that still landed as pop

albums.title: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back
albums.summary: Public Enemy's dense, noisy, political album, produced by the Bomb Squad.

influencedBy.why: Public Enemy came out of the Def Jam scene Run-DMC established, and Chuck D has cited Run-DMC as a model.

cousins.why: Dense, political, and full of overlapping voices

albums.title: Straight Outta Compton
albums.summary: N.W.A's debut, with 'Fuck tha Police', brought West Coast gangsta rap to national attention.

cousins.why: Records that sparked a moral panic

albums.title: Disintegration
albums.summary: The Cure's slow, lush album about depression and getting older.

cousins.why: Long, sad songs that wash over the listener

albums.title: 3 Feet High and Rising
albums.summary: De La Soul and producer Prince Paul's playful album, built from samples of everything from Steely Dan to Johnny Cash.

cousins.why: A playful, colorful album with skits and a loose concept
Gentle, inventive albums that moved a genre away from its rougher roots

albums.title: Paul's Boutique
albums.summary: Built with the Dust Brothers from hundreds of samples, it flopped at first and became a landmark of sample collage.

influencedBy.why: 'The Sounds of Science' samples the Beatles, including Sgt. Pepper's.
The Beasties came up on Def Jam alongside Run-DMC.

cousins.why: Albums built from hundreds of samples

albums.title: No Fences
albums.summary: Garth Brooks' second album, with 'Friends in Low Places', sold over 17 million copies in the US and brought arena-scale showmanship to country.

influencedBy.why: Brooks has said hearing George Strait's debut single in 1981 made him commit to country.

cousins.why: Records that raised the commercial ceiling of their genre
Arena-sized, crowd-pleasing records that sold tens of millions

albums.title: Violator
albums.summary: Depeche Mode's dark synth-pop album, with 'Personal Jesus' and 'Enjoy the Silence'.

influencedBy.why: Depeche Mode has named Kraftwerk as a key influence.

cousins.why: Dark synth-pop with religious and sexual themes

albums.title: Nevermind
albums.summary: Nirvana's breakthrough with 'Smells Like Teen Spirit' brought alternative rock to the mainstream.

influencedBy.why: Kurt Cobain said he was trying to rip off Pixies when writing 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'.
Cobain listed Raw Power among his favorite albums.
Cobain came out of the punk and hardcore scene Black Flag defined.

cousins.why: Breakthrough records that made outsiders mainstream

albums.title: Loveless
albums.summary: Kevin Shields spent years and a fortune on its blurred, bending walls of guitar.

influencedBy.why: Shields cited the Jesus and Mary Chain's noise-pop as a turning point.

albums.title: The Low End Theory
albums.summary: A Tribe Called Quest's second album, with stripped-down jazz samples and Ron Carter on bass.

influencedBy.why: Tribe and De La Soul were part of the same Native Tongues collective, and Q-Tip appears on 3 Feet High.

albums.title: Blue Lines
albums.summary: Massive Attack's debut fused hip-hop, soul and dub into what was later called trip hop.

influencedBy.why: Massive Attack came out of the Wild Bunch sound system, and critics trace the album's bass to dub.

albums.title: Rage Against the Machine
albums.summary: Rage Against the Machine's debut combined hip-hop delivery with metal riffs and radical politics.

influencedBy.why: Zack de la Rocha has named Public Enemy as a key influence.
Run-DMC and Aerosmith's 'Walk This Way' opened the rap-rock path.

albums.title: The Chronic
albums.summary: Dr. Dre's solo debut, built on slow P-Funk grooves and live replayed samples, defined G-funk.

influencedBy.why: 'Let Me Ride' interpolates Parliament's 'Mothership Connection (Star Child)'.
Dre produced N.W.A before going solo.

cousins.why: Lavish, slick production that defined its era's radio

albums.title: Grace
albums.summary: Jeff Buckley's only completed album, with his version of 'Hallelujah' and a soaring, operatic voice.

influencedBy.why: Buckley cited Led Zeppelin as a formative influence, and critics heard Robert Plant in his range.

cousins.why: An unusual voice with huge dynamic range

albums.title: The Downward Spiral
albums.summary: Trent Reznor's concept album about self-destruction, built from noise and samples.

influencedBy.why: Reznor has named Bowie's Low as a major influence.
Reznor has cited Depeche Mode's dark synth-pop.

albums.title: Illmatic
albums.summary: Nas' debut, with production by DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and Large Professor, is often called the best rap album.

influencedBy.why: Nas has named Rakim as a primary influence on his rhyming.

cousins.why: A short, dense body of work that defined its form

albums.title: The Bends
albums.summary: Radiohead's second album, with 'Fake Plastic Trees', moved them from one-hit band to serious songwriters.

influencedBy.why: Thom Yorke said seeing Jeff Buckley perform gave him the courage to sing 'Fake Plastic Trees' in falsetto.
Critics heard the American grunge wave in its loud guitars.

albums.title: Me Against the World
albums.summary: 2Pac's reflective album, released while he was in prison, with 'Dear Mama'.

cousins.why: Autobiographical songs about trouble and a mother's love
Reflective records made during personal crisis

albums.title: Mystic Stylez
albums.summary: Three 6 Mafia's dark, lo-fi debut, a key source for trap and later phonk.

albums.title: Endtroducing.....
albums.summary: DJ Shadow's debut, built entirely from samples, became a landmark of sample-based music.

influencedBy.why: Critics place it in the collage tradition that Paul's Boutique pushed forward.

albums.title: Either/Or
albums.summary: Elliott Smith's quiet, double-tracked songs about addiction and loneliness. It became a key record for later sad-indie songwriters.

influencedBy.why: Smith repeatedly named the Beatles as his favorite band, and critics heard their mid-period harmonies and chord changes.

cousins.why: Sad, inward records that shaped later artists

albums.title: OK Computer
albums.summary: Radiohead's album about alienation and technology, with layered, eerie arrangements.

influencedBy.why: Thom Yorke said Bitches Brew was a key reference for its atmosphere.
The band cited DJ Shadow's sample-built sound as an influence.
The band built on The Bends with more experimental arrangements.

cousins.why: Unease built from atmosphere and texture

albums.title: Supa Dupa Fly
albums.summary: Missy Elliott's debut with Timbaland's skittering, futuristic beats.

albums.title: Homework
albums.summary: Daft Punk's debut, with 'Around the World' and 'Da Funk', put French house on the map.

influencedBy.why: Their song 'Teachers' names Juan Atkins among the producers they learned from.
Critics heard electro's robotic funk in the album.

albums.title: Aquemini
albums.summary: OutKast's third album mixed funk, soul and Southern rap with live instrumentation.

influencedBy.why: George Clinton appears on 'Synthesizer', and the duo has named P-Funk as an influence.

cousins.why: Mixing old and new to change a genre

albums.title: The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill
albums.summary: Lauryn Hill's only solo album mixed rap and soul and won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

albums.title: Kid A
albums.summary: Radiohead dropped guitars for synths, drum machines and processed voices.

influencedBy.why: Yorke said the horn arrangement of 'The National Anthem' came from Mingus.
The band has cited Can's rhythms.

cousins.why: A sharp turn toward electronic sounds
A star retreating into cold electronics

albums.title: Voodoo
albums.summary: D'Angelo's album recorded at Electric Lady with the Soulquarians, with a behind-the-beat groove.

influencedBy.why: Questlove has said the band studied There's a Riot Goin' On during the sessions.
D'Angelo has named Prince as his main influence.

albums.title: Is This It
albums.summary: The Strokes' debut brought scrappy New York rock back into fashion.

influencedBy.why: The band's sound was widely compared to the Velvet Underground.
Critics heard Television's guitars.

cousins.why: Early-2000s New York records that reset their scenes

albums.title: Lateralus
albums.summary: Tool's third album, built on unusual meters and the Fibonacci sequence.

influencedBy.why: Tool toured with King Crimson and has cited them as an influence.
Critics place Tool in the prog line of Yes and Crimson.

cousins.why: Albums meant to be heard as one continuous piece

albums.title: The Blueprint
albums.summary: Jay-Z's album built on sped-up soul samples, many produced by Kanye West and Just Blaze. It set the sound of early-2000s mainstream rap.

cousins.why: Classic Southern soul as the emotional core
Early-2000s New York records that reset their scenes

albums.title: Discovery
albums.summary: Daft Punk's second album, with 'One More Time' and 'Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger', filtered disco and soft rock through robotic vocals.

influencedBy.why: Daft Punk moved from Homework's raw house to more melodic, disco-based pop.

albums.title: The College Dropout
albums.summary: Kanye West's debut used sped-up soul samples and personal, funny lyrics about class, faith and college.

influencedBy.why: West developed his sped-up soul sample style producing for The Blueprint.

cousins.why: Warm, personal songs about ordinary life

albums.title: Barrio Fino
albums.summary: Daddy Yankee's album with 'Gasolina' took reggaeton global.

cousins.why: A regional sound going international in 2004 and 2005

albums.title: Trap House
albums.summary: Gucci Mane's debut album helped define the Atlanta trap sound and its drug-dealing themes.

influencedBy.why: Critics trace trap's dark, 808-driven sound to Memphis rap like Three 6 Mafia.

cousins.why: Regional outsider music that built its own industry

albums.title: Back to Black
albums.summary: Amy Winehouse with producer Mark Ronson and the Dap-Kings revived 60s soul and girl-group sounds.

influencedBy.why: Winehouse took her look from the Ronettes and Ronson's production echoes the girl-group era.
Critics compared her to Aretha Franklin's Atlantic records.

albums.title: Donuts
albums.summary: J Dilla's instrumental beat album, made largely in a hospital bed and released three days before his death. Its loose, off-grid rhythms shaped a generation of producers.

cousins.why: Instrumental mood pieces built from loops
A last work by an artist who died young, revered later

albums.title: For Emma, Forever Ago
albums.summary: Justin Vernon recorded these falsetto songs alone in a Wisconsin cabin. It became an emblem of solitary indie folk.

cousins.why: Heartbreak sung through a processed or strained voice; Vernon later worked with Kanye West

albums.title: Untrue
albums.summary: Burial's album of crackly, pitched vocal samples over shuffling garage beats, evoking London at night.

albums.title: 808s & Heartbreak
albums.summary: Kanye West's album of Auto-Tuned singing over Roland TR-808 drums, made after his mother's death and a breakup. It reshaped hip-hop and R&B.

influencedBy.why: West moved from soul samples to bleak, minimal electronic sound.

cousins.why: Albums made from grief and a breakup
A star retreating into cold, electronic sounds

albums.title: Sigh No More
albums.summary: Mumford & Sons' banjo-driven, stomping debut became a huge crossover hit and set off a wave of folk-pop.

cousins.why: Rootsy songs that reached arena audiences

albums.title: Crack the Skye
albums.summary: Mastodon's prog concept album.

influencedBy.why: Mastodon has named King Crimson as an influence.
Critics placed its long prog-metal suites alongside Tool, with whom Mastodon toured in 2007.

albums.title: My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
albums.summary: Kanye West's lavish, guest-heavy album about fame and excess, made at a studio retreat in Hawaii.

influencedBy.why: 'Power' samples King Crimson's '21st Century Schizoid Man'.

cousins.why: Maximal studio albums as cultural events

albums.title: Cosmogramma
albums.summary: Flying Lotus' dense, cosmic beat album with harp, strings and Thundercat on bass.

influencedBy.why: Flying Lotus has named J Dilla as his main influence.
Flying Lotus is the great-nephew of Alice Coltrane, John Coltrane's wife, and the album draws on their spiritual jazz.

albums.title: Black Radio
albums.summary: Robert Glasper's Experiment brought in R&B and hip-hop singers and won the Grammy for best R&B album.

influencedBy.why: Glasper has repeatedly named J Dilla as a central influence on his rhythms and harmony.
Glasper worked from the loose, behind-the-beat feel of the Soulquarians era that Voodoo defined.

albums.title: channel ORANGE
albums.summary: Frank Ocean's debut album, released after his open letter about a male love.

influencedBy.why: Ocean has cited Stevie Wonder, and critics heard him throughout.

albums.title: good kid, m.A.A.d city
albums.summary: Kendrick Lamar's concept album about growing up in Compton, told like a film over one day.

influencedBy.why: Dr. Dre executive produced it, and Lamar has called Dre's Compton music formative.
Critics widely compared it to Illmatic as a coming-of-age street story.

cousins.why: A continuous album held together by sound effects and theme

albums.title: Pure Heroine
albums.summary: Lorde's minimal debut about suburban teen life, with 'Royals', made when she was 16.

cousins.why: Precise observations from a young writer
Cool, minimal records about youth and nightlife

albums.title: Yeezus
albums.summary: Kanye West's abrasive, minimal album with industrial and acid house sounds, co-produced in part by Daft Punk.

influencedBy.why: 'Blood on the Leaves' samples Nina Simone's 'Strange Fruit' from this album.
Daft Punk co-produced several tracks, bringing their harsh early sound.

albums.title: Random Access Memories
albums.summary: Daft Punk swapped samples for live session players, with Nile Rodgers on 'Get Lucky' and Giorgio Moroder narrating his own track.

Giorgio Moroder, producer of 'I Feel Love', tells his story on 'Giorgio by Moroder'.
The duo turned Discovery's sampled disco into the real thing with live players.

albums.title: Metamodern Sounds in Country Music
albums.summary: Sturgill Simpson's psychedelic, philosophical take on outlaw country, made cheaply in Nashville.

influencedBy.why: Critics widely compared Simpson's voice and approach to Waylon Jennings' outlaw records.

cousins.why: Psychedelia applied to an old form

albums.summary: Taylor Swift's first full pop album, built on 1980s synth-pop sounds with producers Max Martin and Jack Antonoff.

cousins.why: A country songwriter moving toward glossy pop

albums.title: The Epic
albums.summary: A three-hour triple album with orchestra and choir that brought spiritual jazz to a new young audience.

influencedBy.why: Washington has named Coltrane as a primary influence, and critics heard A Love Supreme throughout.
Critics placed it in the spiritual jazz line that Pharoah Sanders carried on after Coltrane.

cousins.why: Washington played on it; both are sprawling, ambitious Black American statements

albums.title: Currents
albums.summary: Kevin Parker shifted from guitar psychedelia to synths and soft disco.

albums.title: To Pimp a Butterfly
albums.summary: Kendrick Lamar's album about race, fame and depression, built on jazz, funk and spoken word with players like Thundercat and Kamasi Washington.

influencedBy.why: Lamar said he listened heavily to Miles Davis while making it, and the sessions were steeped in jazz.
George Clinton appears on 'Wesley's Theory', and P-Funk runs through the album.
It ends with Lamar in conversation with an old 2Pac interview, and he has called Tupac his biggest influence.
Flying Lotus produced 'Wesley's Theory'.
Lamar followed his Compton concept album with a broader look at Black America.

albums.title: Blonde
albums.summary: Frank Ocean's minimal, guitar and organ-based album about memory and love.

influencedBy.why: Ocean stripped back his debut's sound.
Ocean has cited the Beatles; 'White Ferrari' credits 'Here, There and Everywhere'.

albums.title: Lemonade
albums.summary: Beyoncé's visual album about infidelity, healing and Black womanhood, crossing rock, country and R&B.

influencedBy.why: Critics placed its themes of betrayal and self-respect in the line of Aretha Franklin's Atlantic records.

cousins.why: Ambitious statements about Black American life
Albums built around a fractured relationship

albums.title: Purgatory
albums.summary: Tyler Childers' album of Kentucky songs about drinking, faith and love, produced by Sturgill Simpson.

influencedBy.why: Sturgill Simpson produced it and shaped its sound.

cousins.why: Loose, rowdy songs about drinking and redemption

albums.title: Ctrl
albums.summary: SZA's debut, frank about insecurity and relationships.

influencedBy.why: SZA has named Lauryn Hill as a major influence.

albums.title: Golden Hour
albums.summary: Kacey Musgraves added disco, vocoder and soft psychedelic touches to country. It won the Grammy for Album of the Year.

influencedBy.why: Musgraves has named Dolly Parton as a defining influence on her songwriting and image.

albums.title: X 100pre
albums.summary: Bad Bunny's debut album mixed reggaeton, trap, pop punk and more.

influencedBy.why: Bad Bunny has called Daddy Yankee a key influence.

cousins.why: Sung, emotional takes on rap production

albums.title: El Mal Querer
albums.summary: Rosalía's concept album based on a medieval novel, mixing flamenco with R&B and electronic beats.

cousins.why: A concept album about a toxic relationship
Art pop built around a conceptual story

albums.title: When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?
albums.summary: Billie Eilish and her brother Finneas made it in a bedroom; its whispered vocals and bass-heavy production changed mainstream pop.

influencedBy.why: Eilish has named Lorde as an influence, and critics traced her minimal pop to Pure Heroine.

albums.title: African Giant
albums.summary: Burna Boy's album mixing Afrobeats, dancehall and hip-hop, with political themes.

influencedBy.why: Burna Boy has cited Fela Kuti as a major influence; his grandfather was Fela's manager.

cousins.why: A global star with a political message

albums.title: Punisher
albums.summary: Phoebe Bridgers' second album, dark and funny, made her a leading songwriter of her generation.

influencedBy.why: Bridgers has called Elliott Smith her favorite artist, and the title track is about being a fan of his.

cousins.why: Young writers with precise, painful lyrics

albums.title: Whole Lotta Red
albums.summary: Playboi Carti's chaotic, punk-influenced album, divisive at release, became the template for 'rage' rap.

influencedBy.why: Kanye West executive produced it, and critics heard Yeezus' abrasive minimalism.

cousins.why: Chaos and aggression as the point

albums.title: Sour
albums.summary: Olivia Rodrigo's debut, with 'drivers license' and 'good 4 u', mixed teen heartbreak ballads with pop punk.

influencedBy.why: Rodrigo has named Taylor Swift as her biggest songwriting influence.

cousins.why: Young writers with precise, painful lyrics

albums.title: Actual Life (April 14 - December 17 2020)
albums.summary: Fred again.. built emotional dance tracks from voice notes, social media clips and found recordings made during lockdown.

influencedBy.why: Critics compared its chopped vocal samples over garage rhythms to Burial.

albums.title: American Heartbreak
albums.summary: A 34-song album of raw, quickly recorded songs from a former Navy member that made Zach Bryan a major star.

influencedBy.why: Bryan has named Tyler Childers as an influence, and critics placed him in the same raw Appalachian line.

cousins.why: Unguarded songs from a young writer

albums.title: Stick Season
albums.summary: Noah Kahan's album about small-town Vermont life and mental health, which became a major hit after its title song spread online.

cousins.why: Small-town songs that broke through online
Viral songs about specific personal pain

albums.title: Renaissance
albums.summary: Beyoncé's dance album honoring Black and queer club culture, from disco to house to ballroom.

cousins.why: House music made for the dance floor

albums.title: Brat
albums.summary: Charli XCX's abrasive club album that became a cultural moment in summer 2024.

cousins.why: Club music with emotional, diaristic edges

albums.title: Debí Tirar Más Fotos
albums.summary: Bad Bunny's album about Puerto Rico, with salsa, plena and bomba alongside reggaeton.

influencedBy.why: Critics tied its salsa tracks to the Fania era of Celia & Johnny.

cousins.why: Albums about home and the pull of leaving it
Political concern carried by danceable music
